decisive_items: ex vacuo dilatation of the right lateral ventricle
response.rationale: Chronic right hemispheric atrophy with cystic encephalomalacia, gliosis, ex vacuo ventricle, and ipsilateral calvarial/sinus changes indicates a remote early-life focal brain injury, consistent with perinatal stroke. Seizures and left hemiparesis are sequelae. Rasmussen is less likely because it is an active progressive inflammatory process, not a remote focal injury, and onset at 3 months is atypical.

rejected.why: Progressive unilateral atrophy and refractory seizures overlap, but imaging shows remote cystic encephalomalacia/gliosis rather than active Rasmussen inflammation; onset at 3 months and absence of epilepsia partialis continua are atypical.
Hemimegalencephaly is hemispheric overgrowth, whereas imaging shows atrophy and ex vacuo dilatation, not enlargement.
No port-wine stain, leptomeningeal angioma, or cortical calcifications are described; calvarial and sinus changes are nonspecific chronic hemiatrophy findings.
